description: This topic explains how thermal energy moves from one place to another by conduction, convection and radiation, and how these processes are applied and controlled in everyday life.

mcq.questionText: Which process transfers heat through a solid without the particles of the solid moving from one place to another?
mcq.explanation: In conduction, heat passes through a solid by vibration of particles and movement of free electrons, while the particles themselves stay in their fixed positions.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the best conductor of heat?
mcq.explanation: Metals such as copper have many free electrons that carry heat quickly, making them good conductors compared with wood, glass and plastic.

mcq.questionText: Heat transfer that mainly takes place in liquids and gases through the actual movement of the fluid is called:
mcq.explanation: Convection occurs when warmer, less dense parts of a fluid rise and cooler, denser parts sink, setting up convection currents that carry heat.

mcq.questionText: Which mode of heat transfer can occur through a vacuum?
mcq.explanation: Radiation does not need any material medium, so it is the only way heat reaches us from the Sun across the vacuum of space.

mcq.questionText: When a metal rod is heated at one end, heat reaches the other end mainly because of:

options.text: Vibration of particles and movement of free electrons
Light rays passing through the rod

mcq.explanation: In a metal, heated particles vibrate more and pass energy to neighbours, while free electrons move and carry energy quickly along the rod.

mcq.questionText: Which type of surface is the best at absorbing and emitting thermal radiation?
mcq.explanation: Dull black surfaces are good absorbers and good emitters of radiation, while shiny white or silver surfaces are poor absorbers and good reflectors.

mcq.questionText: In a household, why is a heating element placed at the bottom of a water tank or kettle?

options.text: So that heated water rises and sets up convection currents
So that heat is radiated downwards
Because cold water always stays at the top
To prevent conduction through the metal

mcq.explanation: Heating from the bottom warms the lower water, which becomes less dense and rises, while cooler water sinks to be heated, circulating heat through the whole tank.

mcq.questionText: A land breeze blows from the land to the sea during the night because:

options.text: The land stays warmer than the sea at night
The sea cools faster than the land
The land cools faster than the sea, so air rises over the warmer sea
Radiation pushes the air towards the sea

mcq.explanation: At night the land loses heat faster and becomes cooler than the sea; warm air rises over the sea and cooler air flows from land to sea as a land breeze.

mcq.questionText: Why does a wooden spoon feel warmer to touch than a metal spoon left in the same room?

options.text: Wood is actually at a higher temperature
Metal conducts heat away from your hand faster than wood
Wood radiates more heat than metal
Metal absorbs heat from your hand by convection

mcq.explanation: Both are at room temperature, but metal is a good conductor and quickly draws heat from your hand, making it feel colder, while wood is a poor conductor and feels warmer.

mcq.questionText: Which feature of a vacuum (thermos) flask reduces heat loss by radiation?

options.text: The shiny silvered surfaces of the walls
The glass material of the flask

mcq.explanation: Silvered shiny walls are poor emitters and good reflectors of radiation, reducing heat lost or gained by radiation, while the vacuum stops conduction and convection.

mcq.questionText: Air is described as a poor conductor of heat. Which everyday use of air relies on this property?

options.text: Cooking food in a metal pot
Trapped air in woollen clothes keeping the body warm
A car radiator cooling the engine
Heating water with an electric heater

mcq.explanation: Woollen and fluffy clothes trap pockets of air, which is a poor conductor, so they slow the loss of body heat and keep us warm.

mcq.questionText: In the experiment where wax is melted along rods of different metals, the rod whose wax melts farthest first is the one that is the:
mcq.explanation: The metal that lets heat travel along it fastest melts the wax farthest along its length first, showing it is the best conductor of heat.

mcq.questionText: Which statement about radiation is correct?

options.text: It requires a solid medium to travel
It travels as electromagnetic waves and needs no medium
It is fastest in dense materials

mcq.explanation: Thermal radiation is carried by infrared electromagnetic waves that travel through a vacuum and through transparent materials without needing a medium.

mcq.questionText: Why are the cooling fins of a motorcycle or car engine often painted dull black?

options.text: To absorb more heat from the air
To reflect heat back into the engine
Because dull black surfaces emit heat radiation well
To stop conduction through the metal

mcq.explanation: Dull black surfaces are good emitters of radiation, so painting fins black helps the engine lose unwanted heat faster and stay cool.

mcq.questionText: Ventilators are usually placed high up in the walls or roof of a room mainly to:

options.text: Let in cool fresh air at the bottom
Allow warm used air, which rises, to escape

mcq.explanation: Warm, stale air is less dense and rises, so high ventilators let it escape while fresh cooler air enters lower down, keeping good air circulation.

fib.questionText: The transfer of heat through a solid by the vibration of particles and movement of free electrons is called _____.
fib.explanation: Conduction is the main way heat moves through solids, especially metals.

fib.questionText: The movement of heat in liquids and gases caused by the rising of warm fluid and sinking of cool fluid is called _____.
fib.explanation: Convection currents are set up because warm fluid is less dense and rises while cool fluid sinks.

fib.questionText: Heat transfer that does not need any medium and can travel through a vacuum is called _____.
fib.explanation: Radiation travels as electromagnetic (infrared) waves, which is how heat reaches Earth from the Sun.

fib.questionText: Materials that allow heat to pass through them easily, such as copper and aluminium, are called good _____.
fib.explanation: Good conductors, mostly metals, have many free electrons that carry heat quickly.

fib.questionText: Materials that do not allow heat to pass through easily, such as wood and plastic, are called _____ or insulators.
fib.explanation: Poor conductors (insulators) slow down heat transfer and are used to keep things warm or cold.

fib.questionText: A _____ black surface is the best absorber and best emitter of thermal radiation.
fib.explanation: Dull black surfaces absorb and emit radiation well, unlike shiny white or silvered surfaces.

fib.questionText: In a vacuum flask, the space between the two glass walls reduces heat loss by conduction and _____.
fib.explanation: A vacuum has no particles, so it cannot transfer heat by conduction or convection.

fib.questionText: During the day, a cool wind that blows from the sea towards the land is called a sea _____.
fib.explanation: The land heats faster than the sea by day, so warm air rises over land and cool air flows in from the sea as a sea breeze.

fib.questionText: When a fluid is heated, it expands, becomes less _____, and therefore rises.
fib.explanation: Heating makes a fluid expand so its density falls, causing it to rise above cooler, denser fluid.

fib.questionText: Heat reaches the Earth from the Sun mainly by the process of _____.
fib.explanation: Space between the Sun and Earth is a vacuum, so heat can only travel across it by radiation.

tf.questionText: Metals are generally better conductors of heat than non-metals.
tf.explanation: Metals contain free electrons that carry heat quickly, making them good conductors compared with non-metals.

tf.questionText: Convection can take place in a vacuum.
tf.explanation: Convection needs particles of a fluid to move and carry heat, so it cannot happen in a vacuum where there are no particles.

tf.questionText: A shiny silver surface is a poor absorber of heat radiation.
tf.explanation: Shiny silver surfaces reflect most radiation, so they absorb and emit very little heat.

tf.questionText: Warm air is denser than cold air and therefore sinks.
tf.explanation: Warm air is less dense than cold air, so it rises while cold, denser air sinks.

tf.questionText: Radiation is the only mode of heat transfer that does not require a material medium.
tf.explanation: Radiation travels as electromagnetic waves and can pass through a vacuum, unlike conduction and convection.

tf.questionText: Trapped air is a good conductor of heat, which is why blankets keep us warm.
tf.explanation: Trapped air is a poor conductor (good insulator), and blankets keep us warm by reducing heat loss, not by conducting heat.

tf.questionText: In a kettle, water is heated mainly by convection currents.
tf.explanation: Water heated at the bottom rises and cooler water sinks, setting up convection currents that warm all the water.

tf.questionText: Painting a water storage tank dull black helps it absorb more solar radiation and warm the water.
tf.explanation: Dull black surfaces are good absorbers of radiation, so a black tank heats the water inside more effectively in sunlight.

tf.questionText: Heat always flows naturally from a colder body to a hotter body.
tf.explanation: Heat flows naturally from a hotter region to a colder region until their temperatures become equal.

tf.questionText: The vacuum in a thermos flask stops heat loss by conduction and convection but not directly by radiation.
tf.explanation: The vacuum blocks conduction and convection, while the silvered walls are needed to reduce heat loss by radiation.

summary.questionText: Name the three modes of heat transfer.
summary.explanation: These are the three ways thermal energy moves from one place to another.

summary.questionText: Explain briefly how conduction takes place in a metal.
summary.correctAnswer: Heated particles vibrate more and pass energy to neighbours, while free electrons move and carry heat quickly along the metal.
summary.explanation: Both particle vibration and free electron movement transfer heat, but free electrons make metals especially good conductors.

summary.questionText: How is a convection current set up in a heated liquid?
summary.correctAnswer: The warm liquid expands, becomes less dense and rises, while cooler denser liquid sinks, creating a circulating current.
summary.explanation: This continuous rising and sinking carries heat throughout the liquid.

summary.questionText: State two properties of a dull black surface in terms of radiation.
summary.correctAnswer: It is a good absorber of radiation and a good emitter of radiation.
summary.explanation: Dull black surfaces both take in and give out heat radiation well, unlike shiny surfaces.

summary.questionText: Why can radiation reach us from the Sun while conduction and convection cannot?
summary.correctAnswer: Because space is a vacuum with no particles, and only radiation can travel through a vacuum.
summary.explanation: Conduction and convection both require a material medium, which space lacks.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between a sea breeze and a land breeze.
summary.correctAnswer: A sea breeze blows from sea to land during the day, while a land breeze blows from land to sea at night.
summary.explanation: These breezes arise because land heats and cools faster than the sea, changing where warm air rises.

summary.questionText: Describe how a vacuum flask keeps a hot drink hot.
summary.correctAnswer: The vacuum stops conduction and convection, the silvered walls reduce radiation, and the stopper stops heat loss by evaporation and convection.
summary.explanation: Each feature targets a different mode of heat transfer to keep the contents at a steady temperature.

summary.questionText: Give one example of a good conductor and one example of a poor conductor of heat.
summary.correctAnswer: A good conductor is copper (or aluminium); a poor conductor is wood (or plastic, air).
summary.explanation: Metals conduct heat well, while wood, plastic and air are insulators.

summary.questionText: Why are ventilators placed high in a room while openings for fresh air are placed low?
summary.correctAnswer: Warm stale air rises and escapes through the high ventilators, while cool fresh air enters through the lower openings.
summary.explanation: This uses convection to keep air circulating and the room comfortable.

summary.questionText: Compare the three modes of heat transfer in terms of needing a medium.
summary.correctAnswer: Conduction needs a solid medium, convection needs a fluid medium, but radiation needs no medium at all.
summary.explanation: This is a key difference: only radiation can cross a vacuum.

hoq.questionText: A farmer wants to build a simple solar water heater for her home. To make the water heat up as much as possible in sunlight, the metal pipes carrying the water should be:

options.text: Made of plastic and painted shiny white
Made of metal and painted dull black
Made of wood and left unpainted

hoq.explanation: Metal conducts the absorbed heat to the water, and a dull black surface absorbs the most solar radiation, so black metal pipes heat the water best.

hoq.questionText: Two identical cups of hot tea are left on a table. Cup X is shiny silver on the outside and Cup Y is dull black on the outside. After ten minutes, which cup is cooler and why?

options.text: Cup X, because shiny surfaces emit radiation faster
Cup Y, because dull black surfaces emit radiation faster
Both cool at exactly the same rate
Cup X, because silver conducts heat away faster

hoq.explanation: A dull black surface is a better emitter of radiation, so Cup Y loses heat by radiation faster and becomes cooler than the shiny Cup X.

hoq.questionText: In a domestic hot-water system, hot water is taken from the top of the storage tank while cold water enters near the bottom. The best explanation is that:

options.text: Hot water is denser and collects at the bottom
Cold water rises by radiation to the top
Hot water is less dense and rises, collecting at the top by convection
Conduction pushes the hot water upwards

hoq.explanation: Hot water is less dense, so it rises and gathers at the top of the tank through convection, which is why the hot supply is taken from the top.
